## a refusal lists the files the plan allows

ID: `lockstep-guard/a-refusal-lists-the-files-the-plan-allows`

Status: **implemented and tested**

When the edit hook refuses (or warns about) a write to a file the plan does not name, its message SHALL also list the files the plan does allow, read from whichever plan is in use (`lockstep.yaml` `layout:` rows or the planned artifacts of `.aes/target.yaml`): those in the refused file's folder first, at most 15, then "and N more".

## a session replay shows each hand over and read mark

ID: `lockstep-guard/a-session-replay-shows-each-hand-over-and-read-mark`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep replay TRANSCRIPT [--repo PATH] [--store DIR] [--port N]` SHALL serve, on 127.0.0.1 only, a page that steps through one Claude Code or Codex session file in order: the agent's notes, each tool call with its result, each edit hook hand-over as an event of its own, and each read of a requirement page (`generated/wiki/`) or spec (`openspec/specs/`) marked as a requirement read. Each write SHALL carry the marks `lockstep reads` gives that write (file read first, requirement context read first, hand-over, unread), joined by the tool call that made it, so the page and the report never disagree. A Claude session's subagent files SHALL be offered as further sessions. With `--store`, the page SHALL also show each file version a recorder saved there (`timeline.jsonl` and `blobs/<sha256>`); without it, a write shows the text the call wrote. The page SHALL ship inside the package, so an install from git serves it. The session file SHALL be read again on each page refresh, so a running session can be followed.

## a session s writes are listed with what was read first

ID: `lockstep-guard/a-session-s-writes-are-listed-with-what-was-read-first`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep reads TRANSCRIPT` SHALL list, in session order, each write to a file inside the repository (`--repo`, default the current folder) with three marks: whether the session read that file before the write; whether it read the file's requirement context before the write, meaning the `generated/wiki/<capability>.md` page or the `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` of a capability named by the file's `Implements:` lines; and whether the edit hook's requirement text named that file on that write. A write that created the file SHALL be marked `new`: the Write tool's result says so, a Codex file change says `add`, and for a shell write git had not recorded the file on any branch before the second the call was made (outside a git repository a shell write is taken as an overwrite, and an existing file git never saw is taken as new). A file the session wrote whole (the Write tool, or a shell write that created it) counts as read for its later writes. A call that failed before it ran (a refused edit, a hook denial) SHALL count as neither a read nor a write; a delete SHALL not count, and a move SHALL count only its destination. A Claude session's subagent files (`<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`) SHALL be read too, each agent measured on its own reads. Requirement context is found for Python files only, from their docstrings. It SHALL print one warning line for each write to an existing file with neither read, end with `RESULT writes=N new=N file_read_first=N context_read_first=N handover=N unread=N agents=N`, give the same rows as JSON with `--json`, and exit 0 whatever it finds; an unreadable transcript SHALL exit 2.

## agents get the decisions that govern a file

ID: `lockstep-guard/agents-get-the-decisions-that-govern-a-file`

Status: **implemented and tested**

In a repository with OpenSpec specs and a `docs/decisions/` folder, the edit hook SHALL hand an agent that edits a file, or names it in a shell command, each decision record whose `Governs:` line names that file, a folder above it (a target ending in `/` or naming an existing folder), or a requirement or capability the file implements, after any requirement text and without a `permissionDecision`. It SHALL read the record's existing lines only: `Governs:` (or `- Governs:`, comma separated, anchors ignored for paths), `status:` front matter or a `Status:` line, and `superseded_by:` or the text after "superseded by". Each decision SHALL be given as its ID, title, status, file and decision paragraph cut at 600 characters, at most three in full (own path first, then requirement or capability, then folder) and the rest by ID; a superseded decision SHALL be flagged with its successor. The hook SHALL log the decision IDs as `decisions` on the `openspec_text` record. No check SHALL fail on a `Governs:` target that names nothing.

- `lockstep.decisions` — [`src/lockstep/decisions.py:1`](../../src/lockstep/decisions.py#L1)

## an unplanned file is refused where the plan marks it fixed and warned about elsewhere

ID: `lockstep-guard/an-unplanned-file-is-refused-where-the-plan-marks-it-fixed-and-warned-about-elsewhere`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The edit hook SHALL refuse a write to a file under a governed folder that no `layout:` row names when the guard mode is `block`, or when it is `warn` and the file matches a `fixed:` glob. In other `warn` cases it SHALL allow the write with warning context and log `would_block`. In `off` it SHALL skip edit and shell guard checks, including fixed-file checks. The guard mode SHALL come from nonblank `PCW_MODE`, then `guard.mode` in `lockstep.yaml`, then `warn`. Each accepts `block`, `warn` or `off`; bare YAML `true` means block and `false` means off. The hook SHALL use block on invalid input and name invalid `PCW_MODE`. The side-file check SHALL name an invalid `guard.mode`. The template SHALL mark its package folder `fixed:`, so a fresh copy refuses an unplanned source file.

## claude and codex session files are both read

ID: `lockstep-guard/claude-and-codex-session-files-are-both-read`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep reads` SHALL read the four session formats the agents write: a Claude Code transcript and a `claude -p --output-format stream-json` stream (Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit and Bash calls), and a Codex rollout file and a `codex exec --json` stream (command executions and file changes). Shell reads SHALL be found from the command's read commands (`cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed` without `-i`, `nl`, `less`, `grep`, `rg`) or, in a Codex rollout, from Codex's own `parsed_cmd` read entries. Shell writes SHALL be the sure ones the existing shell target parser finds (redirect and tee targets, and what `mv`, `sed -i` and the like write, in a folder that exists); paths that code inside a command merely names SHALL NOT count, because which of them the code writes is unknown. A command's reads and writes SHALL keep the order of its simple commands, and a Codex command's writes SHALL be found even when Codex parsed reads in it. A relative path SHALL be read against the folder the call was made in, and paths SHALL be compared after resolving symbolic links. A record that is not of a known shape SHALL be skipped, never stop the report.

Implemented by:

- `lockstep.read_before_write` — [`src/lockstep/read_before_write.py:1`](../../src/lockstep/read_before_write.py#L1)

- Scenario `a-codex-exec-stream-is-read`: tested by `tests/lockstep/test_read_before_write.py::test_a_codex_exec_stream` ([`tests/lockstep/test_read_before_write.py:138`](../../tests/lockstep/test_read_before_write.py#L138))

## handing over text never approves an edit

ID: `lockstep-guard/handing-over-text-never-approves-an-edit`

## shell commands are judged by the paths they write

ID: `lockstep-guard/shell-commands-are-judged-by-the-paths-they-write`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The edit hook SHALL find the files a shell command writes the way code2check's guard does: redirect and tee targets read as shell words, the files `mv`, `touch`, `sed -i` and the like write, only the destination of a copy (`cp`, `install`, `rsync`), and the paths named by code in the command (a `python -c`, a heredoc script) only when that code calls something that writes; for Python code that parses, only the paths its writing calls target (worked out from string literals, simple assignments and `Path` joins) SHALL count, and Python code whose write target cannot be worked out, or other code, SHALL count every path it names; a `cd` in the command SHALL be followed. In block mode it SHALL refuse a command that writes a file under a governed folder that the plan does not declare, and it SHALL NOT refuse a command that only reads a planned file.

## the replay has a plan code and wiki view

ID: `lockstep-guard/the-replay-has-a-plan-code-and-wiki-view`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The replay page SHALL offer a toggle between its timeline view and a plan, code and wiki view that steps through the same events with the same controls. That view SHALL show the agent's current step; for the file of that step, its `lockstep.yaml` layout row and the text of the requirements it implements (or that no row names it), its code, and the requirement pages and specs the agent has read so far; and a band of hook cards (hand-over, refusal, warning, read marks) marking the ones the current event shows. The server SHALL answer `/api/plan?file=<path>` with that layout row (or null), whether a governed folder and a `fixed:` glob cover the file, and each implemented requirement's id and text.

## the replay shows each write s plan standing requirement progress and the wiki read

ID: `lockstep-guard/the-replay-shows-each-write-s-plan-standing-requirement-progress-and-the-wiki-read`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Each replay write event other than a plan write SHALL carry `planned` (for a shell write, the worst standing of the files it wrote, in the order below): `planned` when a `lockstep.yaml` layout row names the written file and either no plan write in the session names it or one before this write does; `row added later` when a row names it and only plan writes after this one name it; `unplanned` when no row names it and a governed folder covers it; and `outside` otherwise. A plan write names a file when the text it wrote holds the file's path. The timeline SHALL flag an `unplanned` write in orange and a `row added later` write in grey. The server SHALL answer `/api/status` with the note on which test results were used and, for each requirement, its state from `lockstep status`, the files that implement it and the test files tagged with its scenarios; the plan, code and wiki view SHALL show for each requirement whether, by the current step, the session had written none of those files, its code, or its tests, and its state now. The server SHALL answer `/api/wiki` with the paths of the pages under `generated/wiki/`, index first; the wiki pane SHALL list them with the pages read so far highlighted. A file inside a git checkout under the repository (a worktree the agent made there) SHALL be judged, for the plan write and requirement read marks and for `planned`, against that checkout's `lockstep.yaml`, specs and wiki; the session data SHALL name the checkout most of its writes went to, and `/api/status` and `/api/wiki` SHALL take it as `?checkout=`, answering 404 for a folder that is not such a checkout.
